cases.description: Microsoft's example: savings with a present value, at the start of each period
Microsoft's example: a year of payments
Microsoft's example: payments at the start
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: a rate of 0
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: a type of 2 is payment at the start of each period, as PMT-008 found it is for PMT
A number of periods that is not a whole number: 1+rate is raised to it as e^(nper ln(1+rate)), which gives Excel's double; a correctly rounded power is two units in the last place from PV-005's
A negative number of periods: 1 over 1+rate raised to 10 by squaring, which gives Excel's double; squaring 1/(1+rate) is 19 units in the last place away
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: at a rate of 0 a number of periods that is not a whole number is answered, no power being raised

At the start of each period: the payment multiplies (1+rate)*((g-1)/rate), Excel's grouping; multiplying the payment by 1+rate first is one unit in the last place below Excel's (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/)
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: thirty years of months, nine squarings
A type of 0.5 is payment at the start of each period, as PMT-009 found it is for PMT
A quarter period past a whole number: e^(nper ln(1+rate)), as FV-006's half period is

A negative number of periods that is not a whole number: 1 over the power to 10.5, as FV-007's -10 is 1 over the power to 10; raising to -10.5 directly gives the same double here (FV-022 is where they part)

With a present value and a payment, at the start: the sum as written, where fusing pv*g, or the payment's product, into a multiply-add gives 2900.6645063063966 (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/, Search.cs, F4, F9 and F10)
As FV-014, over 240 periods: the sum as written, where a fused multiply-add gives 123950.02507801352
Half a period: the square root of 1+rate, correctly rounded, as the ^ operator takes it (ARITH-133), where e^(0.5 ln(1+rate)), FV-006's evaluation at 10.5, gives 45.62798304316633
A third of a period at a rate below -1: the odd root of a negative 1+rate, as the ^ operator's =(-8)^(1/3) is -1.9999999999999998 (ARITH-043), where e^(nper ln(1+rate)) has no answer
No periods at a rate of -1, where 1+rate is 0: 0 to the power 0 is #NUM!, as the ^ operator's =0^0 is (ARITH-041), where squaring gives 1 and FV gave 500 before the second area pass

At the end of each period, with a present value and a payment: the sum as written, where a fused multiply-add of pv*g into it gives 483.06382918288557, and of the payment 483.0638291828854 (Search.cs, F4, F9 and F10)
Half a period before, at a rate of -1: 0 to a negative power is #DIV/0!, as the ^ operator's =0^-1 is (ARITH-042)
Ten periods before, at a rate of -1: 0 to a negative power is #DIV/0!, as FV-020's is
A negative number of periods that is not a whole number: 1 over the power to 2.5, as FV-007's -10 is 1 over the power to 10, where raising to -2.5 directly gives -247.828794185625

Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: e^(nper ln(1+rate)) with the exponential and the logarithm correctly rounded, as XNPV-013 found them, gives 1154.2771752172287; glibc's exp and log, which .NET takes on Linux, give 1154.2771752172332

Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: half a period before is 1 over the square root of 1+rate, a negative number of periods being 1 over the power to its absolute value (FV-022) and half a period the square root (FV-016); 1 over e^(0.5 ln(1+rate)) gives -38.29015278650261
